title: Chicken Thighs – Slowly Cooked With Garlic Butter
description: Based on a Slow Cooker recipe by Sarah DiGregorio: The seasoning of this rich garlic and herb braise is inspired by escargot butter, which famously makes everything delicious, and is easy to make with just a few ingredients. A generous dollop of sour cream added before serving brings it all together and makes it feel a little fancy. Top bowls generously with croutons, which lend crunch and soak up the flavorful sauce, or maybe big wide noodles.
ingredients: 1½ to 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs, in big chunks
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into chunks
8 large garlic cloves, smashed and chopped
⅓ cup chopped fresh parsley, plus more for serving
Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and pepper
½ cup sour cream or Crème Fraiche
1 bag (2 or so dry cups) spinach
Homemade or store-bought croutons, for topping
directions: Quickly sauté the chicken chunks in hot melted butter for about 2 minutes.

Add the garlic, parsley, beans, lemon juice, 2 teaspoons salt, and several generous grinds of pepper in a Dutch Oven or similar oven pan with a lid. (If it looks too dry, you could add a little water, or chicken broth, or white wine, or vermouth.)
Cook until the chicken is tender and the flavors have mellowed, about 1 ½ hours, checking after the first hour.
A little before you think it’s ready, stir in the spinach and let it wilt for a minute or so. Stir in the sour cream.
Serve the stew topped with croutons and more parsley.
